preamble: The Mayan glottalized uvular stop qʼ, canonically an ejective [qʼ], is often realized as an implosive. Bennett (2016) notes that most ejective–implosive variation in Mayan involves the labial bʼ and the uvular qʼ, while kʼ and tʼ are usually stable ejectives. For Uspanteko, Bennett, Henderson & Harvey (2023) coded 139 tokens of qʼ from nine speakers (eight from San Miguel Uspantán, one from nearby La Lagunita): 53 were implosive [ʛ̥] and 86 ejective. Word-final position favoured the ejective, and speakers differed in how often they used each variant. Wikipedia describes the same variation for Tzʼutujil, where the implosive is possible only before vowels, and Sakapultek, where it is free variation, and gives the implosive as the usual value of qʼ in Kaqchikel and Mam. Most sources describe the implosive as voiceless [ʛ̥], not voiced [ʛ]. Only Wikipedia's Tzʼutujil table gives voiced ʛ, so the cell's symbol is an approximation. This is synchronic variation, not a completed sound change.

languageExamples.context: Variable in all positions; word-final position and a preceding stressed vowel favour the ejective

examples.note: Bennett, Henderson & Harvey (2023). Labial bʼ was implosive in 171 of 214 tokens; velar kʼ was ejective in all but one.

languageExamples.context: Before vowels, alternating with the ejective; only the ejective occurs before consonants and word-finally

examples.note: Wikipedia's inventory lists ʛ ~ qʼ, with the implosive voiced. In the same position it gives bʼ and tʼ as voiced implosives outright.
Wikipedia, citing Mó Isém (2006): /qʼ/ may also be heard as an implosive [ʛ̥] in free variation.

languageExamples.context: Glottalized uvular, reported as implosive [ʛ̥] varying with ejective [qʼ] (Russell 1997, cited by Bennett, Henderson & Harvey 2023)

examples.note: Wiktionary transcription. Wikipedia, citing Patal Majzul et al. (2000), says bʼ and qʼ are usually implosive in Kaqchikel, while tʼ, kʼ, chʼ and tzʼ are ejective.

languageExamples.context: Glottalized uvular, reported as implosive [ʛ̥] varying with ejective [qʼ] (Russell 1997, cited by Bennett, Henderson & Harvey 2023)

examples.note: Wikipedia's Mam inventory and Wiktionary's entry for the Mam letter qʼ give ʛ̥ as the value of qʼ; the ejective–implosive variation itself is reported by Bennett, Henderson & Harvey (2023), citing Russell (1997).
